node.accessibleName: Daytona: Spot GPU sandboxes are now live for everyone! Run GPU workloads on preemptible capacity at a fraction of on-demand pricing: • No quotas: spot GPUs don't count against your GPU quota. Available capacity is the only limit. . • Deeply discounted: significantly cheaper than on-demand GPUs, see the pricing page: [ https://www.daytona.io/pricing (link)] . • All GPU types: H100, H200, RTX Pro 6000, RTX 4090, RTX 5090, with ordered fallback between types. . Getting started: choose a GPU, set resources, and use any Docker image: sandbox = daytona.create( CreateSandboxFromImageParams( image="nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04", auto_delete_interval=0, spot=True, resources=Resources(gpu=1, gpu_type=GpuType.H100), ) ) Heads up: spot sandboxes are preemptible. They can be reclaimed at any time when on-demand capacity is needed, so design workloads to tolerate interruption. Preempted sandboxes get a spotEvictedAt timestamp and stay retrievable for 24 hours. Try it: [ https://app.daytona.io/ (link)] Docs: [ https://www.daytona.io/docs/sandboxes#spot-gpu-sandboxes (link)] Questions? Drop them here or at [ support@daytona.io (link)] saluting face emoji. 8:38 AM. 4 links.

Not a feature request, but hopefully useful. I spent a few weeks benchmarking Firecracker guest images and published the harnesses: github.com/GautamTalksDev/mayfly-guest Main finding: most published kernel-stripping advice for Firecracker is stale. Turning ACPI off costs 278ms rather than saving time, because modern Firecracker passes device info through ACPI tables and MPTable booting is now deprecated. Disabling PCI breaks root disk discovery entirely, since CONFIG_PCI is required for guest A

daytona.io/docs/en/secrets No we do not have this yet, but there is a workaround using tailscale

How we support static egress IPs: The recommended approach is to use a VPN connection with Tailscale and route your sandbox traffic through an exit node you control with a known static IP. From your firewall's perspective, all sandbox traffic will originate from that single IP — giving you full control over what to allowlist. This works out of the box in Daytona since Tailscale falls back to TCP when UDP isn't available. Full guide here: daytona.io/docs/en/vpn-connections#…
